summary: Pad both sides of text to a minimum width.
documentation: center returns a padded string when width exceeds the string length. The optional fill character must contain exactly one character; the default is a space. Widths at or below the existing length leave the text unchanged.
inputs: An object with text, a nonnegative integer width, and a one-character fill string.
returns: A centered string at least width characters long.
caution: Width counts Python string characters, not terminal display columns. Wide glyphs and combining marks may look misaligned even when their string length is correct; center does not truncate long text.
scenarios: Center a heading in a plain-text export with decorative padding.
Make small fixed-width labels in a local report preview.
Create aligned text fixtures when display width is known to be simple.
title: Pad a plain-text heading
problem: Return text.center(width, fill). Preserve text when it already meets or exceeds width, and use the provided single-character fill. Apply Python’s standard centering behavior.
hint: Pass width and fill directly; do not slice text to make it fit.
goal: Use str.center() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
